scope: Scratch-only kernel feasibility; no maintained edits, commits, pushes, issues, scheduler composition or Codex builds.

outcome.first_determining_case: inconclusive: supervisor automatically removed action group between first populated=1 and next observation; absence was not accepted as zero
outcome.incremental_retry: Actual action cgroup populated=0 observed five times before first explicit Frida script/session/manager close, with root plus real setsid descendant, two actual RLIMIT_AS-denied allocation waiters in each process.
outcome.fresh_case: Same result after empty Java class output directory and fresh C worker compilation.
outcome.process_status: Root exit 137 and adopted detached descendant -9 retained by actual supervisor; every recorded PID absent, all owned cgroups removed.

diagnostic_boundary.kill: Direct write of 1 to action/cgroup.kill from Java main thread; not LinuxSupervisor.terminate or a conforming queue cancellation composition.
diagnostic_boundary.supervisor_retention: /usr/bin/kill -STOP stops dedicated supervisor, with its /proc status T verified before action kill, preventing automatic action-cgroup deletion. After zero and instrumentation close, -CONT resumes supervisor; ownership remains constructing-thread confined. Production needs an owner API/protocol retaining the cgroup through observation, not helper-thread use of current owner.
diagnostic_boundary.frida: Sessions/scripts remained owned and installed at kill, and all four waits were in native GCond parking. No script/session/manager unload was invoked before zero. Probe did not force an indefinitely held PTRACE_EVENT_EXIT stop, and does not prove Frida was still holding exit tracing at the exact zero observation.
diagnostic_boundary.barrier_json_field: instrumentationCloseInvoked=false is the state at barrier receipt publication, before the success branch calls closeInstrumentation; driver exit 0 and RESULT prove that branch returned.

primary_kernel_contract.population: For a non-root cgroup, populated=0 means no live process in that group or any descendant; updates are recursive. Zombies are excluded.
primary_kernel_contract.kill: cgroup.kill sends SIGKILL through the subtree with concurrent-fork and migration handling.
primary_kernel_contract.ownership_requirements: All workload tasks must be contained before release and prevented from escaping; controller must prevent unrelated future admissions into the subtree through unload/cleanup. Missing group, empty PID list, root Z state or pending signal is not a substituted zero proof.
primary_kernel_contract.alternative_if_zero_unavailable: Retain hooks and owned cleanup state; require an authoritative complete task barrier, such as whole-subtree frozen=1 plus enforced no-thaw/no-escape/no-new-admissions until cleanup. This alternative was not run or accepted in this slice.

limits: Native diagnostic gate only; no production scheduler/cancellation lifecycle accepted.
No hidden cgroup visibility, memory admission, cross-platform or Cargo/Bazel claim.
A zero observation only supplies execution-impossible proof under complete workload containment and no subsequent admissions; it does not mean every zombie was reaped.
Actual parent and adopted exit results were obtained after hooks closed and supervisor resumed.

cleanup.local_scratch: Retained for parent acceptance; compiled local diagnostic output and newly acquired source input retained only as receipt artifacts.
cleanup.late_retention_request: Parent requested VM retention after SSH exit and hosted post cleanup had already completed; reported unavailable, no replacement dispatched.
